node.statement: Fix k>=2. Once nodes 1.1 and 1.3 are validated, instantiate node 1.3 with R=P_j, T_0=Q_[1,k-1], T_1=Q_k, and T=Q_[1,k]. Node 1.1 supplies every hypothesis of that instance: R,T_0,T_1,T are uniformly accurate Hermitian projections, T=T_0+T_1 exactly, and T_0,T_1 are uniformly approximately orthogonal. Hence the canonical second-index assembly map S_{P_j,Q_[1,k-1]} direct-sum S_{P_j,Q_k} -> S_{P_j,Q_[1,k]} is a bounded complex-linear bijection; its inverse gives the bijection in the direction stated in node 1.4.1.
